llcFilesWith: Tennessee Secretary of State (Application for Registration of Assumed Name, SS-4402)
soleProprietorFilesWith: Not filed with the Secretary of State; the state assumed-name registration is for entities (LLCs, corporations, LPs), and Tennessee has no statewide DBA registry for sole proprietors
feeBasis: The $20 Secretary of State fee registers an assumed name for an LLC or corporation. The registration lasts five years and renews for another $20.
renewalRule: Renewable in successive five-year terms (Application for Renewal of Registration Assumed Name, SS-4481, $20), and § 48-249-106(d)(5) opens the renewal window only within the two months preceding expiration. Changing or cancelling an assumed LLC name is SS-4229, $20; under § 48-249-106(g) the Secretary of State cancels the right to the assumed name if it is not renewed before it expires or if the LLC dissolves.
protectionNote: Registering an assumed name discloses the name an entity trades under; it grants no exclusive trademark right. It does carry a practical effect: because § 48-249-106 screens new names against assumed names as well as true, reserved, and registered names, an active assumed name blocks a later entity or assumed name that is not distinguishable from it.
searchNote: Assumed names registered by entities appear in the Secretary of State's business search alongside the entities themselves, since they are part of the same distinguishability records.
notes: Tennessee publishes no free official copy of its code: the General Assembly's own 'Tennessee Code' link hands off to lexisnexis.com/hottopics/tncode and no state host carries the code text, so the mirror citations below are kept under the README exception with the enacted Public Chapters (read in full 2026-08-06 from the Legislature's own PDF archive) as the corroborating official source. Tennessee's assumed name is an entity filing: an LLC or corporation registers one $20 assumed name with the Secretary of State, good for five years and renewable. Sole proprietors are not part of this system, and there is no newspaper-publication requirement. Because assumed names sit in the same records the state screens for distinguishability, a registered assumed name behaves defensively like an entity name while it is active.
